A1.evidence: Single complete file, lines 1-1631; all sprites are string arrays (125-276), sound is Web Audio (56-107); no external resources, no placeholders.

A2.evidence: result.json: loads_clean true but survives_play false with one pageerror 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)' at 54.6s. Cause: render line 1501 computes frame with EXPL_BIG.length (4) for every explosion, line 1502 indexes EXPL_SMALL[3] which does not exist (EXPL_SMALL has 3 frames, 266-270); drawSprite(undefined) throws at line 281 on arr.length. The throw happens inside loop() before requestAnimationFrame(loop) at line 1621, so the game loop stops permanently. Screenshots 4-play-060s and 4-play-075s are pixel-identical (frozen).

A3.evidence: Fixed FIXED_DT = 1/60 (655); loop() accumulates real time, clamps to 0.1 s and runs update(FIXED_DT) in a while loop (1608-1622) on requestAnimationFrame (1621, 1624).

bugs.text: Console error 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)': render computes the explosion frame with EXPL_BIG.length (4) for every explosion and indexes EXPL_SMALL[3], which does not exist. drawSprite(undefined) throws on arr.length. The throw is inside loop() before requestAnimationFrame(loop), so the whole game loop stops. Every Zako or Goei kill (and every captive death, dual-half loss and challenge hit) produces a small explosion, so the game freezes within 0.3 s of nearly any kill (screenshots 4-play-060s and 4-play-075s are identical; survives_play false).

The player cannot fire during a challenging stage: the Space handler only fires when state is PLAYING, and the challenge runs in state CHALLENGE. Hits are always 0, the stage is 12 seconds of waiting, and the 100/1000/10000 scoring can never happen. P (pause) is likewise ignored in the challenge (612).

Rescue and dual fighter never trigger: destroyEnemy clears captiveAlive at 1180 before testing captiveAlive && mode === 'diving' at 1186, so freeCaptive is dead code and shooting a diving boss with a captive just destroys the captive.

A boss that fires its tractor beam is set to mode 'beam', which updateEnemies never handles. The boss stops swaying and, if the beam misses, stays frozen at that spot for the rest of the stage (never dives or returns to formation). The beam also fires from the formation row rather than after a partial dive.

Capture ignores the post-respawn invulnerability and happens instantly with no pull-up animation; a player can be captured again within a frame of respawning. The beam roll (0.001 per boss per frame) makes beams very frequent.
The captive sprite is positioned once at capture and only updated while the boss dives, so it stays fixed while the boss sways in formation.
Boss Galaga always scores 150; the 400/800/1600 diving and escort values are never awarded.
Stage badges draw one badge per denomination <= stage (stage 7 shows '1' and '5'), not the arcade's sum of denominations.

Challenge stage: all 40 enemies spawn at once, each row's 8 start at the identical point and move at the same speed so they overlap as one blob, they wrap around forever instead of flying through, the stage ends on a 12 s timer, and the wave bonus is approximated as floor(hits/8)*1000.
No 'STAGE N' card and no stage jingle before a challenging stage; setupStage returns before entering STAGE_INTRO.
Entry is 40 solo streams from random x positions with 0.15 s spacing, not grouped formations along shared paths.
When a boss finishes its dive its escorts are teleported to y=-20 and set to 'returning' even if they are mid-path.
Title score table lists Boss Galaga as 150/400 only, omitting 800 and 1600.

summary: The file is cleanly organised (state object, update, render, fixed-timestep loop) with readable names, pixel-art string sprites, a proper starfield, HUD, title table, localStorage high score, two-hit colour-changing bosses, bezier entries and dives with escorts, and a full set of synthesized sounds, so at a glance it looks like a credible Galaga. In play it collapses: the explosion renderer indexes a fourth frame of a three-frame small-explosion array, which throws and kills the requestAnimationFrame loop, so the game freezes within a third of a second of shooting almost any Zako or Goei; the headless run confirms the freeze. Beyond that, the signature mechanic is hollow: the tractor beam fires from formation, the boss then sticks in an unhandled 'beam' mode, the rescue branch is dead code so the dual fighter can never appear, the captive never fires, and the challenging stage cannot be shot at because Space is gated on the PLAYING state. Boss scoring, badges, formation breathing and grouped entries are all simplified. The skeleton is faithful; the game is not.
